record.context_brief: classification of affine structures on T^3
record.original_question: How can one classify affine structures on the 3-torus T^3?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.13. How to classify affine structures on \(\mathbf{T}^3\)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An affine structure on a smooth manifold $M$ is a maximal atlas of charts with values in $\mathbb{R}^n$ whose transition maps are restrictions of affine transformations of $\mathbb{R}^n$ (elements of $\mathrm{GL}(n,\mathbb{R})\ltimes\mathbb{R}^n$). Equivalently, it is a torsion-free flat affine connection on $M$. To each such structure on a connected manifold one associates a developing map $\mathrm{dev}\colon \widetilde{M}\to\mathbb{R}^n$ and a holonomy homomorphism $\rho\colon\pi_1(M)\to\mathrm{Aff}(\mathbb{R}^n)$, well defined up to conjugation. Two affine structures are equivalent if they are related by a diffeomorphism of $M$ preserving the affine atlases (isotopy is also a natural equivalence).

Let $\mathbf{T}^3=\mathbb{R}^3/\mathbb{Z}^3$ be the 3-dimensional torus. Provide a classification, up to equivalence, of all affine structures on $\mathbf{T}^3$ (not assumed complete), describing the moduli space of such structures together with their holonomy representations $\rho\colon\mathbb{Z}^3\to\mathrm{Aff}(\mathbb{R}^3)$ and developing images.
artifact.status_search_result: Complete affine structures on $\mathbf{T}^3$ were classified by Fried–Goldman (1983) within the framework of three-dimensional affine crystallographic groups, and analogous results in dimension 2 are classical (Nagano–Yagi). However, a full classification of all (not necessarily complete) affine structures on $\mathbf{T}^3$ remains an open problem; no comprehensive moduli description has been published, and the question is repeatedly cited as open in surveys on flat affine structures.

status_evidence.title: Three-Dimensional Affine Crystallographic Groups (Fried–Goldman)
status_evidence.snippet: Classification of complete affine structures in dimension three, including those on T^3 in the complete case.
status_evidence.claim: The complete case of affine structures on T^3 is classified, but the non-complete case is not.

status_evidence.title: Flat affine, projective and conformal structures on manifolds (Goldman)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing classification problems for affine structures, noting open questions in dimension 3.
status_evidence.claim: General classification of affine structures on T^3 remains an open problem.

status_evidence.title: The affine structures on the real two-torus (Nagano–Yagi)
status_evidence.snippet: Classification of affine structures on T^2 obtained by Nagano and Yagi.
status_evidence.claim: The two-dimensional analogue is solved; the three-dimensional analogue remains the natural next problem.
